What was said yesterday about those 260-odd documents, yes, but I would like to ask the Chamber at this moment is that when Mr. Ruez begins to testify, I would like the Prosecution to be guided by what we now have in the 65 ter list so not to go beyond the documents that were disclosed and classified according to the usual practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I don't know if that would be acceptable in all cases with Mr. McCloskey but I suppose every effort will be made to standardise the introduction of exhibits in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, if I could just take a minute to find that podium and move over so I -- I'm hiding from Judge Stole at the moment. I would like to move, if I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The other thing now before the witness comes in, we finished with Mr. Hasic's testimony. I take it that the Prosecution does not wish to tender any documents as exhibits arising from his testimony? Any of the Defence teams would like to tender any documents? Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I would like to tender a document which has now received a document 5D18. It is a list of members of ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I take it there has been no opposition on the part of the Prosecution, so this document is tendered and so admitted as Exhibit -- Defence Exhibit 5D00018. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will also tender by e-court a list of our documents for cross-examination, just for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Soljan, if she is still here -- no, I don't think she is still here. All right. Is there any objection on the part of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So tell Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: For the sake of completeness, there were three documents put to the witness during the course of his evidence, 7D12, 7D13 and 7D14. We will highlight the passages for the court officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. And the understanding is the same as before; it is definitely not our intention to allow the introduction of evidence which is not evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So please do highlight the parts that you want to tender as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We understand fully that the purpose for which it was put to the witness and the effect it has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If that is at all necessary because the passages have been read and question has been put to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whether he confirms his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The other thing is this: This is why I'm raising this matter, whether it's necessary or not, but I will leave that in your discretion, Mr. Haynes. Problem that may arise is the following: At least in one of them, that's the 6th one, one of the statements, 1996 one, 6th - I forget the month, 6th of December or something like that - there is a reference to certain individuals who were protected witnesses and whose names should be in any case redacted if we are admitting this or that statement or other statements into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, we will have regard to that. I hear the Prosecution -- I haven't heard -- I don't imagine the Prosecution have any objection to those passages as it were becoming part of the documentation in the case. We will review whether we strictly think it's necessary given the way in which the passages were read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and appreciate that. Perhaps you could also contemplate tendering that particular page where the -- where the front page where there is the signature of -- or the last page and that particular page or those particular pages where the extracts read out to the witness are and nothing beyond that. Perhaps that would help us sort out the practical problems that may arise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Consider it done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. While we are on that subject, we understood that that was going to be the practice as from a few days ago when it came up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And one of the reasons we did not object to that process is that that will help our process as well when we have our witnesses so -- and I -- so as long as that when we have a witness that we use a statement to impeach them or to remind them of something, if that comes in as evidence as well. Now, this will be important because I will anticipate that a witness may say, "I never said that accused A was there." And we will come back and say, "Well on such and such day of so and so, you previously testified that he was there." And so we will then offer that piece of statement into evidence as substantial evidence, as they are doing here. And so equality of arms, if that's the rule we are ready to go with it. I just want to make sure that's the understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought we made that clear, that that particular excerpt from the statement would go into evidence for whatever it is worth. Not necessarily and exclusively for the purpose it's being made use of either by your side or by the other side. So that's the -- that has been the practice in this Tribunal in any case. So if it's not clear enough we will make it clear and I take the responsibility for not having made it clear enough if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think it's clear but Mr. Bourgon and I speaking on issues related to that had some differences and if he was here perhaps we would, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you are a US citizen and he is Canadian. So that explains the misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We will try to stay away from the US, if we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So can we safely introduce Mr. Ruez in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A correction. The list I mentioned, it is related to cross-examination of Jean-Rene Ruez, not the particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because you did not make any use of documents but I was not sure. Thank you. Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If I could briefly tell Your Honours what we had in mind, if we could leave Mr. Ruez out for one second, please, not that I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before he starts making speeches.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Exactly. The CD that we have spoken of of these 200 some-odd photographs that we believe reflects the 65 ter numbers, I was able to get actually quicker than I had imagined just a colour copy of those. Now, of course this is not in evidence. It does not have numbers yet. But it is convenient for us that are used to this. I unfortunately only had four so I have one, Mr. Ruez will have one. I've given two to the Defence and I've asked if they would give one to you but they've refused so -- but I don't know. You'll be seeing all these photographs on the screen, Your Honour, and it is our intention that after we get through the admissibility stage of this to be able to provide the admissible documents with the numbers and just the outline so you can tell where they fit in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Last thing before Mr. Ruez comes in, yesterday we enjoined you and actually we also stated it in your written decision to explain to Mr. Ruez the concerns expressed previously which are the basis of our decision and the substantives of our decision. I take it that you have done so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I've had a chance to do that the last break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so it is my intention to call Mr. Ruez. We will then basically be just going through the crime scenes and he'll have videos that he shot with little video clips.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I will be explaining to Mr. Ruez that the procedure adopted in this Trial Chamber is somewhat different to the ones he's been -- he's used to, namely, that it will be a strict question and answer and then it's only when it is indicated to him that he's got a licence to expand that he will be able to do so and always under the control, strict control, of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's a good idea. I explained that and I told him many of my questions will be yes or no and I'll ask him why and we needed to have limited, direct responses to that and we'll see how it goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and I'm grateful to you, Mr. McCloskey. Let's bring in Mr. Ruez, please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Ruez, and welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're familiar with these proceedings. You've worked here, you've testified. So we'll go straight to the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fine. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable. This is the fourth, fifth time that you are giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 6th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Each Trial Chamber has its own way of procedural method. The method that we adopt in this Trial Chamber is a little bit different to the ones adopted when you previously testified both in Krstic and Blagojevic in particular. And namely that the procedure we intend to follow is a strict question and answer one. You will be examined in chief by Mr. McCloskey first. He will be putting to you a series of questions, some of which or the majority of which I would say would require a simple yes or no answer, in which case please just stick to a yes or a no. And then there will be several other questions where you will be asked to go further than that and expand and explain. So you will be directed both by Mr. McCloskey and by ourselves as we go along. The same applies when you are cross-examined by the seven Defence teams that we have here. I do wish also to make it clear to you that you will be here testifying for quite a long time. So I hope you've made all the arrangements necessary because you'll be here the rest of this week, certainly the whole of next week, and incidentally we will not be sitting on the 13th next week because we've got a plenary and in addition, we agreed to make an arrangement with the Prlic Trial Chamber to accommodate the testimony of an important witness who would otherwise not be available before at least six months from now. So there will not be a sitting on the 13th, and if you're not finished by the 20th, then on the 20th, also, we have a plenary, another plenary, and there will not be a sitting. So I'm just telling you so that you are prepared and it's in your interest to try and get out of here and go back to your work the earliest possible. At the same time, we require from you all the information and assistance that you can give us based on the intelligence and information that you have collected in the course of your investigations. So I give him straight to you, Mr. McCloskey. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, Ms. Stewart just reminded me, we all have a little list of potentially sensitive witnesses, survivors. I don't intend to be asking a lot of questions about them but in the course of examination in-chief and cross-examination, these names may come up. Mr. Ruez has the same sheet and it may just be simpler to refer to their 65 ter number. If there is any issue we can go into private session but everyone is agreeable to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Provided that this document is not made public itself and provided that there is no other document in the records which are publicly open, available to the public, which would show relationship between the 65 ter number and the name of witnesses anywhere. Just make sure of that. Otherwise we can live with it and I suppose that it is okay with all the Defence teams. I see no objection by anyone. So let's move ahead. You've understood the point made by Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perfectly well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, will you state your full name and spell your last for the record?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: My name is Jean-Rene Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How do you spell your last name?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: R-U-E-Z.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is your current profession?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I am a chief superintendent at the French Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you describe for us what that job is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I'm currently working at the international technical police cooperation service at the headquarters in Paris.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in the hierarchy of police services in France, can you just give us just a rough background of where that fits?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: They are three groups of superintendents, there were, named commissaire, commissaire principal, and commissaire divisionnaire. I am commissaire divisionnaire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are familiar with the police we see in Paris. Where are you compared to the police, the traffic police and the police that we are all used to seeing, the Gendarmerie?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In this specific work, there is no relation to Metrovidone [phoen], but previously I was working in judicial police, before joining the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's get to that. First of all, after your secondary education, can you outline the education you went through?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I first did my military service, going through the military school of Saint-Cyr Coetquidan so I served as a reserve officer. I finished with the rank of Lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How long were you in that service?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's a one year compulsory military service in France. It was at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: And I continued in the reserve during two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What was next?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Then I joined the university to study law. I finished that, obtaining a law degree, named maitrise in France as well as two certificates of the institute of criminology in Paris.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was the name of that university?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The name is University Paris II Assas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you give us an idea of the length of your study to obtain those degrees?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Maitrise you get it in four years and the two certificates in one year. So I studied in total for five years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: After your education what did you do?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I passed the contest to join the national superior police school that is in Lyon. It is the training school for the French superintendents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you pass that school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How long was that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's a two year long training and then you start working in the branch that you have selected and I selected judicial police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: As you can see, my boss is telling me to slow down back here. We need to hesitate, as you know. That's for the translation. Okay. Can you tell us a bit about the judicial police and where that fits in in the hierarchy of French police forces?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Judicial police has as a main task to deal with the most serious crimes and mainly with organised crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me help you a little bit. Judicial police is distinguished from the executive police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Executive police, I don't know what the translation is, sir, in French, but in France the police is separated in several branches, namely public order, public security, general information services, counterintelligence and then judicial police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. So now you were -- you know where you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what year did you join the judicial police?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That -- the judicial police in 88.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you briefly describe your career?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: My first posting was as a deputy chief of judicial police station in Paris, in the 18th district. Then I took the head of a unit named research unit at the 4th division of judicial police in Paris.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just tell us briefly what that unit did.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a kind of a special police force dealing not once a crime has been committed but working in advance of a crime, trying to collect information of the potential perpetrators and infiltrate their groups, if necessary, and then arrest them before they commit the crime or just after.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: After that, I joined the regional criminal service based in Marseilles as deputy head of the banditisme repression brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And tell us a bit about that job?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is mainly designed to solve cases connected with attacks on banks and financial institutions for armed vehicles carrying -- armoured vehicles carrying funds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as a deputy head, what kind of responsibility did you have?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Follow all the operational activities of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And how long did you do that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In Marseilles less than a year because then I took the posting of a head of that same type of group but named banditisme repression group. That was an antenna of that regional criminal service based in Nice and covering the French Riviera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how long did you have the Nice job?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Until the 7th April 1995 when I arrived in The Hague to join the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you explain how that -- were you -- did you become a UN employee, were you seconded, can you explain that situation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I replied to an offer made by the Ministry of Interior requesting volunteers among the corps of superintendents, in order to fulfil a demand that was made by the Tribunal to the French government at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So who was paying you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I was paid by the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was your relationship with your police force in France?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Let's say that my career still would continue in France but I was fully -- I was paid and had no more relationship with France except paying my pension fund.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you promoted along the normal lines by the French forces?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. My career continued in that sense as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But you were under the direction of the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: During all the years I did spend at this Tribunal, yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And how long did you work for the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: From 7 April 1995 through 7 April 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in April 2001, can you briefly outline what you've done up until the present which you've already told us about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I took a leave of absence, without working, resettled on an island in the French Caribes named Guadalupe and returned to my normal activity, let's say, in July 2003, where I joined the international cooperation service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now let's talk about, I guess it was the spring of 1995, when you became a member of the ICTY, the Office of the Prosecutor. What was your first general assignment?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Upon arrival, I was tasked to join an investigative team that was busy with the investigation related to the siege of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did that change at some point within a few months?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it did. Once the fall of Srebrenica occurred, a lot of press rumours were hitting the Office of the Prosecutor, and it was then decided to send a few people in the area where refugees were arriving, that is Tuzla, and I was designated to go there and make an evaluation of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And shortly thereafter were you designated the head of the Srebrenica investigation or something like that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: During one and a half years, I continued being busy with this case but without any structure around. I mean not a formal structure. And the team was created early 1997 to deal full time with this investigation but that was not the case before early 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did I come in in October 1996 to become part of the Srebrenica group with you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: You were indeed the first reinforcement of our little investigation force available before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then once you got a more formal group around you, did you stay the chief of the Srebrenica investigation through the -- 2001 when you left?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I changed position from a P3 investigator into P4 team leader and that was early 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, have you at our request been able to assemble basic crime scene and key area photos and videos in order to present some of that material for the Court over the next few days?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is this basically the same material that you have presented in the last two trials?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Most of it, yes, but I didn't prepare this presentation by using the binders of the previous trials. I didn't have time for that. So I used the database of some 2000 pictures that I have from all the missions we did and made a compilation of these, trying to select as less pictures as possible to show the places where the events occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, did that include assembling some video footage?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, that included the assembling of videos. All of these videos have been shown in the previous trials. I just made an effort to compress them so they would take a little less time because I know this Chamber is willing to reduce the time of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are trying but we may be having the opposite effect but that's not anyone's fault. That's just the nature of the proceedings but we will try to get through this as efficiently as we can. All right. Well, then, do you have in front of you the book, a book containing some of those -- well, all of those photographs and maps?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And they have been, as you're aware, put into an electronic system called Sanction. You unfortunately under this system cannot write or change anything, so I will sometimes endeavour to have you explain from the photograph in which way Potocari is or such things but we will do that individually. And the Court has heard already quite a bit about the facts of the case so I won't be asking you to reiterate those in much detail for context, so let's start with your -- the first thing that you've chosen to create, and I will be trying to remember the actual number. The exhibit, the overall exhibit number is P02103, and we will be just going from 1 to 271. So let's go to page 1 of this exhibit. You can -- should be able to see it on your screen. And can you just -- this is obviously a map of the area with Srebrenica highlighted. What was the purpose of that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a map that covers more or less entirely the area where important scenes are located, and the aim is only to show the general area and the distances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Is this map to scale?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is to scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let's go to page 2, then, the next page. And we see a picture of a town. Can you briefly explain what this is and what direction we are looking at it in?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a picture I took during the summer 1997. It is designed just to show to the Court how the town of Srebrenica looks like, sandwiched in between two large hills, and it's a long stretch of buildings, and this area is showing direction north, knowing that the Bosnian Serb army entered through the direction shown on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So as we look into this photo, direction north, the next little town of significance on your map is what? Mr. Ruez, the next town up from this point. We haven't got to that photograph yet but just to help orient the Court. The next town beyond this one --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Going -- going north in the direction of that photograph, goes towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to number 2.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This one is a helicopter view, showing the town but seen from the opposite direction from north towards south, and this picture that was taken in summer 1998, shows the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So is this the urban area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is part of the urban area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Is there some part we can't see from this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The part that is more south so at the bottom -- north, sorry, so at the bottom of the picture.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please make pauses between questions and answers? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. At this time, I note on your outline you have a short video. Can you tell us briefly what the significance of the video is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The video is designed to show the area south of Srebrenica from where the Bosnian Serb army entered the town and also show the town in its extent, not only with these two photographs, they don't show the total size of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall when this was shot?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That was a helicopter flight that I did in 1998, summer 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's make it -- make it clear that when the witness says the video is designed to show the area south of Srebrenica from where the Bosnian Serb army entered the town, you were not there when the Bosnian Serb Serbian army entered the town, were you, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No I was not on the spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's not taken as testimony that that is indeed the area from where the Bosnian Serb army entered the town. I assume that will be confirmed by other evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I think most everything Mr. Ruez will be saying today will be confirmed by other evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. What I wanted to do is put the Defence minds at rest that that is not being taken as evidence. That will allay their concerns. Let's move ahead. Thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this video is our 65 ter number 1514.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, can you speak over the blade of the helicopter, roughly how far south of the town is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a few kilometres south of the town, approximately three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is this the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What is this we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a company B, that is a UN base in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That was apparently a little slow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we need to go back a couple of stills and if we could have a reference, I think the video would have a counter that would refer straight to the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the question refers to the building shown at still 01 minute 38 seconds point 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I think you stated this was the Srebrenica UN base at the time of the events; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's the so-called bravo company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in particular, it's the building right adjacent to the building with the long red roof?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct that at one point one could see UN markings on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We'll see that a little later in another video, I think. Okay. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This shows the direction of Potocari that is just behind this big hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And roughly how far is Potocari from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Depending on where in Srebrenica, since the town is stretched. I will assume four or five kilometres, no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now let's go to your next exhibit which I believe is a map, number 4? And what -- what is the purpose of this illustration?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Since the population took two courses of action, this one is showing the direction that most of the men took from Srebrenica towards an area that is northwest of the enclave, named Susnjari where the men assembled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And again you've learned that from your investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And these little yellow dots with letters on it, what is that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: These dots mark the position of the UN observation post that were along the separation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we see in the middle, UN bravo company with a little red corner. Is that roughly where it's located in Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, correct. This is marking the rough position of this building we saw on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then as we go north we see UN base. What's that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the main UN base, that is in a factory in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next one, which I believe is 5. And what does this show?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the same map than the previous one, but now indicating the direction that took some of the men and mostly the women and the children, so towards the area of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next shot, which is 6. Excuse me, we have a short video clip. So let's go to that before we get -- can you stall that for a second. Just tell us what this clip is about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This clip is showing the distance between Srebrenica and Potocari, so it just continues at the point the previous one had stopped. So behind this hill will be Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did the investigation reveal that this was the path that many of the women and children took at they walked towards Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the path that more or less all of them took, either by foot or on board of trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So let's continue with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: For the record this video clip is 65 ter 1545. I know we'll have other exhibits but can you briefly describe what this is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. This is a grouping of factories where many refugees took shelter into, those who could not enter the main base.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. McCloskey. For the record, the buildings that the witness was referred to were at still 0 minute 42 seconds. Is this the same video as the one before or a new one or a different one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a very different one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what do you mean by different?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is the continuation of the other one. The previous one was showing Srebrenica town and part of the way towards Potocari. This one is showing Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But it's the same helicopter flight?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is the same flight, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm asking because presumably you flew over Srebrenica before you flew over Potocari.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we started that flight from the south towards the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So following that, the counter would show a reading which is beyond that that we saw when you were flying over Srebrenica which was 1 minute something and here we are only 42 seconds, not even reached one minute, so perhaps -- I mean I know for sure that there should be an explanation of that but if it's a continuation of the previous video, I would imagine the counter would show -- unless the counter is separate from the video itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which is the case I'm being told by --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's my understanding. This is Sanction doing the counting and that I don't think we had a counter working at the time but Mr. Ruez may know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That explains the difference.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Another explanation is also the fact that I took many bits out of this long video because the entire flight lasted one hour and 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's perfectly clear. Go ahead, Mr. McCloskey, and regulate yourself. I mean we should be having a break in about six, seven minutes time but we can have it a little bit later or earlier should you so wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for reminding me about the counter. We are now at a still at 0042.3 and there is a building in the centre of this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That large structure is the so-called express compound. It was a compound that was used by a bus company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. As we look in the right-hand corner of this picture, what building is up in the right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This building is the so-called blue factory, that is a factory that is just before the main base, the UN base.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, let's continue and we'll get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are at still 1 minute 06 seconds point 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Unfortunately it's on a blurry shot. But could you point out the -- this house that the Court has heard about, the so-called White House, if it's on this shot?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I regret not having a mouse but if one looks as a reference point the road, in the middle of the picture, under the road, at the right-hand of the road going north, is what I named as the blue factory, and just in front of this blue factory, opposite side of the road, so a bit more middle up of the picture, is a white dot on this fuzzy picture, but this is the so-called White House.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The arrow we see on the dark side, on the black side of the screen could be moved around and then the witness can tell us stop there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, stop there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Live and learn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Someone knew exactly where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. If we could continue the film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So stop there. Stop there. And we are at one minute, 15 seconds point 8. Mr. Ruez, the building you referred to before, is it the small building that we see on the screen on the left-hand side of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The mouse can probably follow that. Yes. Thank you, if we could continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Stop right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we are now at 1 minute 25 seconds point 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What's this big, long rectangular building?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This large building is the so-called Akumulator factory. It was a former battery factory used by the UN battalion as its main base.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we could continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This might be a good time to take a break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. We will have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could go to the next image, which is number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, what we have in front of us is a black and white image, with yellow on it. Can you first of all tell us what is this black and white image and where did the investigation get it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The black and white image is an aerial photograph that was obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor from the US State Department. And the yellow markings were added for the sake of the trial of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, the Office of the Prosecutor obtained the black and white portions of the photograph, including the labelling overview, Potocari, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the date 13 July; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, that was originally obtained under Rule 70 but was cleared for courtroom use; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, there are certain constrictions placed on this photograph by the United States government, and that is that you're allowed to refer to this as what?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: As aerial imagery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as part of United States' surveillance systems, if I recall correctly?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Reconnaissance systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, reconnaissance systems, thank you. And as for anything else based on that, the United States has not provided us the authorisation to speak about it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And the yellow material you put on yourself?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No. These ones were done for the sake of the trial of General Krstic and I was not the one who added the labels.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. The OTP has done that. Okay. All right. You've obviously flown over Potocari. Looking at this as an image or a photograph, do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you just briefly go over the yellow markings and tell us what they represent?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the top of the picture, it is the direction south. The first arrows mark the buildings where the refugees took shelter. We have seen them on the film. The express bus compound and at the right of the picture, two factories, one being the so-called Zinc Factory and the other one the 11th of March factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And as we go down farther on the picture?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: As we go down, is the blue factory, so-called blue factory; in front of it, alongside of the road a building named from its company, Feros.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Any particular significance from the investigation of those two buildings?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We, as far as we know, these ones were not used as a shelter by the refugees. This area had been cordoned off by the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Then we see the White House marked. That's the same White House we spoke of before?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is, as well as the UN base in this main building, the Akumulator factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that yellow square around the UN base, as far as you know, does that reflect a perimeter or is it just a rough guideline?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is the perimeter of the base as it was used at that time by the UN battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then let's go to the next photograph, which is number 7. Again, we see in a white circle that's the White House; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The white circle is indeed the White House.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the blue box?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The blue box shows the UN base.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go to number 8. Now, what's number 8?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Number 8 is a photograph that I took in January 1996. It was the first photograph that we could take of the so-called White House in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you -- was this the first time you were actually able to get to the area of the events?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were you -- can you just describe, was it a regular investigative mission or what were you able to get done on this mission with the snow on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We used the opportunity of a visit to the area of Mr. John Shattuck who at that time was an Under Secretary of State for -- I don't remember exactly what his title was at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: US official of some sort?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, US official, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So we used the opportunity to expand a bit his mission, that was initially designed to show the completion of Dayton agreement in terms of freedom of movement in that area, and we went to several spots, including north, the Grbavci school, so-called Grbavci school and more on the south, the soccer field of Novaka Sava. We also had access for the first time at the warehouse close to Kravica. We made a short stop at a suspect mass grave area named Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get to some of the photos on those places as well. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Shattuck was Under Secretary of State for human rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the security situation on the ground for you at the time?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: For this mission, the escort was provided by state security of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did that consist of?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: If I recall well, three to four bodyguards or two of them, and one vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And this photograph, this is a close-up of the White House?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let's go to the next photograph, number 9. This is a split image. And can you tell us the -- the bottom image appears to be similar as the last one, a winter time shot; is that correct, of the White House?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. The split is designed to show the location where the man on the balcony are sitting, that is an extract of the video filmed at the time of the events by the journalist named Zoran Petrovic and the arrow shows the rough area where these prisoners were sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: To give a brief explanation, you say the video of Zoran Petrovic, can you tell -- just when did the Office of the Prosecutor obtain the first version of the Petrovic video, roughly, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I don't remember very well. That might have been by the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this portion of it when the men on the balcony, was that part of what was obtained originally?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Negative. There were parts of it that we named the missing pictures, a few footages that had been cut off of the original video, prior that second version be sold to journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And so after you left the OTP, are you aware that the OTP received a copy of some of the missing footage?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I learned that from Dutch journalists who went to see me on my island in Guadeloupe and who showed me for the first time the missing pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This symbol in the upper right-hand corner of the top of picture, got a B around it and circles, do you know what that means?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, this is the logo of Studio B.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's what?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a so-called independent radio or television from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will go into much more detail with other witnesses on this particular aspect but not -- it's not my purpose to deal with Mr. Ruez in too much detail on that because we do have much more detailed analysis that you will see. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could -- let's go to the next photo. Number -- if we -- actually, we have a -- another short video, which is numbered 65 ter 1557. Mr. Ruez, can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is again a helicopter views from the same flight I talked previously, showing at this moment Potocari and the road that goes north towards Bratunac town and gives a quick idea of the small size of the town of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So at 3, 1, point 2 that cluster of buildings in the distance is what you're referring to as Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, Your Honours, we have a 36-minute film which is a compilation of video obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor. Some of it under Mr. Ruez's watch, others of it after his watch. It's a good time to just play it I think. We have just about enough time to do it. I won't be asking him much because that will -- that may cause us to be a bit delayed but -- and there will be other witnesses that will speak in more detail about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The problem is the other trial that we would be delaying. All right. It will be more than that because it's five -- it's 20 past now so it will be five to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can cut it short, too. You'll be seeing a fair amount of this video, I think, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go ahead and see how we can -- because I don't know what video it is so maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Much of this video will be video that was shot at the time by combat cameras, by news cameras, by Muslims. You'll see that it's all labelled and self-explanatory, to some degree you'll have questions and we will get through it and go from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At least we will get through part of it, a substantial part of it. The thing is I wouldn't want to delay the start of the next trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I sit down during this? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, do you recognise this man in this picture at 5/4/point 3?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise him as being Colonel Vinko Pandurevic, commander of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, do you know what that man is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I was told he's Major Jolovic, nicknamed Legenda who is heading a unit attached to the Zvornik Brigade named the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, is this the UN base that we saw a photo of that you described earlier in the helicopter video?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct. And when the video was taken in 1998, the signs, "UN Srebrenica," were erased from the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's at 6.43.2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, do you know where the location of this building that those people are inside is, at 17.21.6?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a hangar inside the main base at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you, Mr. Ruez, at 20.30.1, start from the right and, if you can identify anyone that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At this moment, in the middle of the picture is as everyone knows, General Mladic. At the right of the picture, one can see again Colonel Pandurevic. Then again at the right is one man who I suppose is one of the bodyguards of General Mladic. Just behind General Mladic, I cannot see the face of the person but at his left is another bodyguard of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the -- we'll try to keep the video going to see if we can get the physical of the person?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now we see a face behind General Mladic. Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Just at the left of General Mladic is General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And now we are at 20 minutes 31 seconds point 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, they don't get the APC out and it might be a good time to stop. They try for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Maybe they will succeed tomorrow. Yes. I think we will stop here so that we don't keep the other Trial Chamber from being able to start its trial on time. I thank you for all your cooperation. We will reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 8th day of September, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
